title: Saving a new part number renames the part in place
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin who can switch between two locations: the test location and location B.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location and at location B under the same part number, with 3 in its default bin at the test location.
  • Set part A's Sell Price to a new value once before the test, so its Part History already has an entry.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Type the new number in the Search box.
  6. Click the clock icon (Part History) at the left of the part A row.
  7. Click Parts in the top bar.
  8. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  9. Type part A's old part number in the Search box.
  10. Replace the search text with the new number.
  11. Click the row for the new number.
  12. Pick location B in the location selector at the top right.
  13. Click Parts in the top bar.
  14. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  15. Type the new number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The window closes and the change is saved.

Step 5:

  • One row is listed: part A under the new number, with the same description and the same bin with 3.

Step 6:

  • Part History still shows the earlier Sell Price entry, plus a new entry "Part number updated | Original number:" with the old number, then "| New number:" with the new number: it is the same part, with its history kept.

Step 7:

  • The Parts left menu shows Part Library.

Step 8:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 9:

  • No entry has the old number any more.

Step 10:

  • Exactly one entry has the new number: no new entry was made.

Step 11:

  • The entry's Parts table lists both the test location and location B under Workplace.

Step 12:

  • The location selector shows location B.

Step 13:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 14:

  • Location B's Inventory page opens.

Step 15:

  • At location B part A also reads the new number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • S10-R23: “A changed part number writes "Part number updated | Original number: {old} | New number: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “A part's number and description can be edited from the part dialog. The change is made to the part's own Part Library entry, which every location that stocks the part shares.”
  • Key Decisions: “The number and description are shared. They live on the part's Part Library entry, which every location that stocks the part shares. Editing them at one location changes them at every location, and the dialog says so before the save (S13-R12, S13-R16).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
